subject.title: [security] External provider skips SSH credential destination validation

question: What trusted approval mechanism should External SSH destination validation use when repository config selects external.connection.ssh.host and authentication is inherited or ambient?
rationale: The missing guard is source-reproducible, but the approval mechanism affects External provider compatibility and Crabbox's documented repository-config trust boundary.

options.title: Reuse trusted-source approval
options.body: Treat trusted user config as approval, reject repository-selected External SSH destinations with inherited or ambient auth, and allow repository-contained same-source key pairs.

options.title: Add explicit External SSH override knobs
options.body: Introduce dedicated trusted flag or environment approval for External SSH host/key destinations, matching Static SSH and Parallels ergonomics at the cost of new configuration surface.

options.title: Document and defer hardening
options.body: Leave current behavior in place temporarily and document that repository External connection config can steer inherited SSH authentication, accepting the security-boundary risk.

recommendation.title: Reuse trusted-source approval
recommendation.body: Treat trusted user config as approval, reject repository-selected External SSH destinations with inherited or ambient auth, and allow repository-contained same-source key pairs.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the adjacent policy and credential-destination history and is the clearest routing point for the External-specific boundary choice.
